quest.title: Like Rhyme and Song, the Summer Reverie
quest.description: To find out the truth, everyone returns to the location of the mysterious machine to investigate.
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x30, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

chapter.title: Like Rhyme and Song, the Summer Reverie

talks.objective: Head to the location of the Fatui machine

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, look! Isn't that the same guy we saw on our first day here?

dialogues.speaker: Researcher
dialogues.text: Ahaha... *hic* Everyone's gone crazy. Everyone should get out of here!

dialogues.speaker: Researcher
dialogues.text: We'll... We'll never wake up... But I was right, my precious, you are invincible... hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: Precious? What's his precious?

dialogues.speaker: Researcher
dialogues.text: A miracle machine... Definitely not... impossible... *hic*!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: I think he's referring to that machine.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: What a drunkard, hmph.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Oh goodness, the smell of alcohol... Mein Fräulein, please allow me to fan the fumes away with my wings.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Excellent, please fan them away for me, too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Me as well.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Certainly.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: I've checked the surroundings, but there's no one else here.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Isn't that strange? The Fatui is a big organization, but he is the only one left at this camp. What's more, we didn't even see him the last time we were here.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Even the larger gentleman from the first time is missing. I think... they must be hiding somewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: As for why they may be hiding, I'm afraid we'll have to ask him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But he's as drunk as Tone-Deaf Bard... Should we wait for him to sober up?

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Cleanse him with the holy spring of punishment!

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Mein Fräulein means to splash him with water.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like a good idea. Let's try!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Everyone takes out their water bottles and empties them over the collapsed Fatui researcher...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, he opened his eyes!

dialogues.speaker: Researcher
dialogues.text: Hm... Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Hey, are you one of the Fatui? Can you tell us what happened here and what that machine is for?

dialogues.speaker: Researcher
dialogues.text: ...F—Fatui...

dialogues.speaker: Researcher
dialogues.text: ...Hah! Fatui!

dialogues.speaker: Researcher
dialogues.text: Oh... those blockheads from the administration will regret it now! Haha! That's what you get for rejecting my research and forcing me to...

dialogues.speaker: Researcher
dialogues.text: Forcing me to... to conduct my research on this deserted island... My precious! My precious... *sobs*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why is he crying? Looks like he has a lot of pent-up emotions...

dialogues.speaker: Researcher
dialogues.text: ...You mocked me... and my precious invention! You... you don't know anything about the future.

dialogues.speaker: Researcher
dialogues.text: Only my invention... can help us conquer the world! Haha... hahaha...

dialogues.speaker: Researcher
dialogues.text: Idiots, such idiots, hahaha...

dialogues.speaker: Researcher
dialogues.text: Ow! Don't hit me! I won't blow up the lab again... I'm sorry! I didn't mean to...

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: This man's gone insane. There's no way we can communicate with him.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: He wasn't like this when we first met him. It looks like the effects have grown worse, to the point of driving him mad.

dialogues.speaker: Researcher
dialogues.text: *sobs*... My manuscript, my manuscript! Only that... can save... save... *sobs*

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Manuscript? Where is it?

dialogues.speaker: Researcher
dialogues.text: Don't yell at me, don't yell at me... *sobs*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Fischl, don't yell at him!

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Hmph! Then I'll...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Let me try.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Kind sir, look at me. Now tell me, where did you hide your manuscript?

dialogues.speaker: Researcher
dialogues.text: *sobs* No, no, don't force me to write a report... *sobs* Go away...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, he's completely lost in his own imagination...

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Allow me.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Please excuse me!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Kazuha stands quietly for a while, then throws the researcher over his shoulder and onto the ground.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Haah!

dialogues.speaker: Researcher
dialogues.text: *sobs* Ow! My butt... *sobs* My brain is finally starting to work again... It's not a mushy mess anymore...

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Can you tell me where you put the manuscript?

dialogues.speaker: Researcher
dialogues.text: The manuscript... the manuscript... is in the crack over there...

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: Whew, finally! Otherwise, I was gonna have to blast some of my loudest rock 'n' roll in his ears.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kazuha hesitated for a long time before making a move. He's so nice.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yup. He's destined for greatness.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Everyone, let's search the stone cracks nearby for the manuscript.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Found it!

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Congratulations! We've found the key to solving the problem!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Let me see... Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Mona takes the manuscript and studies it carefully...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Just as I thought. This machinery named "Cognitive Mimicry" is capable of altering the state of people's brains. It was invented by the researcher we met earlier, his name is Persikov.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: According to the manuscript, the Fatui officials did not support Persikov's research. They believed he had taken the wrong path.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: But Persikov insisted on putting his machine to use. In order to achieve that, he disassembled the machine and used his connections to transport the parts to this deserted island.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How did they find this island? The Fatui's intelligence network's not to be underestimated.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Persikov was dead set on carrying out his experiments on this island. Most of his subjects were junior Fatui soldiers who all signed a waiver before the experiment.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: ...It looks like they really thought this machine would benefit the Fatui.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: How does the machine work?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: That's most likely top-secret. The manuscript didn't reveal any details, but Persikov did mention that the machine was modeled after the power of a god.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Does that mean... there's a god connected to these dream-like mirages, and the Fatui found a way to research it?

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Clearly. Otherwise, they wouldn't have been able to reproduce the god's power.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Wait, so there's some sort of... Mirage Archon?)

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Anyway, Persikov's experiment did not go as planned. The machine broke down just days after it was activated. They tried to fix it, but...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: The technologically illiterate Fatui soldiers completely ruined the machine. Even its most important component of all — the crystalline cores — got ejected and disappeared.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: A testament to the importance of maintenance in all aspects of life. I believe we can all learn something from this.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Persikov may be a mad scientist, but he didn't want to see his subordinates suffer. Besides, if he didn't solve the problem, he would end up going insane as well.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: As a last resort, Persikov went out on his own to look for the cores. But he was just a sickly researcher unfit for the task. He had to give up.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Then, Persikov went searching for the soldiers who had gone mad and strayed from the group, and took them to a hidden cave.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: I think that was where they were at the day we arrived on this island. Persikov was taking a strong Fatui soldier somewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Yes. It took Persikov all of his strength to get all the missing soldiers into the cave. He tried to snap them out of it with music and poetry...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: But nothing worked.

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: We came here once but there was no one around. Come to think of it, that must've been the day Persikov was busy gathering the soldiers into the cave.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: There's good news and bad news written on the last few pages.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: The good news is, Persikov managed to figure out the location of the crystalline cores by piecing together the snippets of information he could get from the delirious soldiers...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: The bad news is, Persikov failed to revive them, and eventually succumbed to the device's influence himself. The last few pages of the manuscript are just unintelligible drunken scribbles.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: It appears that the responsibility for this issue now falls to my retainers and I.

choices.text: Never thought we'd be saving the day on a vacation...

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: There's a map in the manuscript. The markings should indicate the locations of the crystalline cores.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We've got no choice but to find the crystalline cores now!

choices.text: I feel a sense of purpose.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The researcher came to his senses briefly after Kazuha's throw, but soon fell unconscious...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Did his mental state deteriorate, or did Kazuha knock him out...?)

talks.objective: Insert the Crystalline Cores into the machine

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've inserted all the crystalline cores. Mona, is that all we needed to do?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: I think so. That's what the manuscript says anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Let's give it some time. Hopefully, it'll return to normal.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Everyone sits around the campfire, chatting and cooking barbecue.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Once the machine is fixed, the situation seems to improve. Soon, you hear footsteps approaching...

dialogues.speaker: Fatui Sergeant
dialogues.text: Aah! Someone's in our camp!

dialogues.speaker: Fatui Recruit
dialogues.text: Hey, who are you people!?

dialogues.speaker: Fatui Sergeant
dialogues.text: Hold on, look at the machine... is it fixed?

dialogues.speaker: Fatui Recruit
dialogues.text: What? But Mr. Persikov is still lying on the ground over there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're the ones who fixed the device. Yeah, you're welcome!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: We could have had a nice, relaxing vacation, if all of this hadn't ended up occupying so much of our time.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Hmph! Apologize to me and my retainers at once!

dialogues.speaker: Fatui Sergeant
dialogues.text: Huh!? Oh no, oh no, I—I'm outta here...

dialogues.speaker: Fatui Recruit
dialogues.text: Hey, hey! Don't leave me here on my own... Mr. Persikov's still there, we need to save him!

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: Haha, those two definitely seem a little more lucid now.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: It looks like we succeeded.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yay! Let's get outta here then. Paimon wants to spend the rest of this vacation back at our own camp.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You mean Klee's camp.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! But it feels like our camp now, kinda like our temporary home, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Then perhaps we should call it the Embassy of the Immernachtreich and Dodoland.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? No! That's too many words. Paimon would prefer something easy to remember.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Come on, let's go home now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *yawn* Whew! After coming home to a nice big meal then having a long lie down, Paimon's finally starting to feel relaxed.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Hehe, is the hospitality of the Immernachtreich to thy liking?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's loving it!

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Wonderful. Mein Fräulein invited you all here not only to witness the arrival of our Holy Land, but most importantly, she wished that you could all relax and enjoy the summer.

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: Great! Well, I've come to the right place — I love it here!

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: May this place become an eternal paradise.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Mein Fräulein says she hopes to go on more adventures with you here in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: Of course! And you should come find me in Liyue when you get the time. I'll show you around.

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: Oh, also, my friend runs the best restaurant in Liyue. I'm sure you'll love it.

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: If you're into opera, you should go see Yun Jin. She's the nicest person, and she likes making friends with new and interesting people. I'm sure the two of you will have plenty to talk about with your shared passion for theatrics.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Oh? If Lady Xinyan speaks so highly of it, then I must entertain the idea.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, I have a suggestion.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: There is a snack called Roasted Lavender Melon in Inazuma, which goes rather well with fish. Why don't we roast some fruit and seafood for dinner tonight?

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: Then it's decided. I'll go gather some more fruit. And for seasoning... Yup, that should do it.

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: Ah, you're all here.

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: I've noticed an issue. Although we've fixed the machine, as you can see — the mirages on the islands have still not disappeared.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: I've noticed that, too. But considering it took some time for the mirages to appear, it may also take some time for them to disappear.

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: Yes, that's definitely possible.

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: In other news, my scryglass seems to be working fine now. The divination results are also looking about right, although...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Although what?

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: Although there are some parts in the results that I don't quite understand... it's as if there is some sort of power surrounding us, and it's still watching us.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: Do you think it's caused by the machine, or perhaps Persikov?

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: Sorry, I'm also not sure. All I know is that the power is not hostile at the moment. Whatever it is, it doesn't seem to harbor any ill will toward us.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (That reminds me, there's one unanswered question on these islands. But the group is unaware.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'll keep that in mind.

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: Well, although there's nothing left to disturb us, and we can finally kick back and enjoy our vacation, we still ought to be cautious while we're on these islands.

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: I will keep seeing what the stars say every day.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: I promised Fischl that I'd be her guard. I can help.

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: Good, I'll be counting on you.

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: ...*sigh* Goodness knows why those girls are so carefree about everything. I suppose it falls to me to be extra vigilant.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Paimon, come with me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, coming!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's go over there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohh, so we're gonna call the Tone-Deaf Bard, right?

response.speaker: Dodocommunication Device
response.text: Dodoco! Dodoco!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Well hello there, strangers! You finally called! I thought you were having so much fun that you'd completely forgotten about me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nope! Tone-Deaf Bard, a whole bunch of really strange things happened!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Venti everything that has happened on the islands over the past few days...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: A strange machine that can imitate the power of a God? Wow, haha, I didn't know the Fatui had plans like that. Their imaginations are truly running wild.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So judging from your tone, it sounds like you don't know any more about this than we do?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Alas, I am but a humble bard who sings for his Mora in the tavern. Why would I know anything about it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, so annoying...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: But, other than that, did you two have fun?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We did! We ate a lot of yummy food and saw loads of amazing things. It was really cool!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Hehe, that's good.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: The point of traveling is to record any feelings stirred along the way. As long as you had an unforgettable experience, this journey has served its purpose.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: As for the mysterious voice, although we don't know who it was, not only did she not harm you, she also helped you to gain a better understanding of each other, right?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: If you look at it that way, maybe she meant you well. I mean, if she was able to intercept Alice's communication tool, I'm sure she's also plenty capable of attacking you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, Tone-Deaf Bard is right...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I understand.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Hahaha, I'm glad to bring you some peace of mind. Just enjoy your vacation to the fullest, and don't forget to tell me all about the marvelous mirages when you get back.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: I want to record all these beautiful memories, and turn them into ballads. Every summer will become an unforgettable song.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's a deal.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: #Then I'll just wait for your return, {NICKNAME}. Happy vacationing!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If Tone-Deaf Bard thinks it's okay, then maybe there's nothing to worry about.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: After all, Tone-Deaf Bard is still a god. We should probably trust him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's head back, we don't wanna keep everyone waiting.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hold on, didn't Fischl say earlier that she's going to catch some crabs? Paimon wants to go too!
Now you have solved the mystery... doesn't it make you feel happy, satisfied?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (That voice...!)
Don't worry, I won't hurt you. I'm just a little bird that sometimes flies by these islands, and am now watching you from far, far away.
I just so happened to sense a power here that has something to do with me. I was curious, so I landed on the beach to quietly watch everything that took place on these islands.
...It was fascinating. The ones who came here to work were so busy, and yet I still saw genuine smiles on their faces from time to time.
And then all of you arrived later on, bringing your glorious dreamscapes and wonderful willpower.
Your dreams are like the pure and delicate bubbles floating on the water. The more beautiful the illusion, the more it fascinates me.
I'm not able to travel myself, but I do admire free spirits like yourself. So I helped them design a little something for you all. I hope you liked it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Who are you?
As I said, I don't have an agenda. I'm just a little bird. I stopped here to admire your lives — joys, sorrows, and all.
You are a special person, with a unique and brilliant glow. I decided to communicate with you in this way because I'm really curious about you.
There is no need to wonder about my name. Maybe one day in the future, we will meet in another place.
When that time comes, I think you'll be able to recognize me. Hehe.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (The voice has faded... Was she directly speaking into my mind?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, what are you doing? The crabs don't catch themselves!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (...What did she mean...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ("Meet in another place"... But when, and where?)

choices.text: Overall, I'd say it was pretty satisfying.
Roasted Lavender Melon sounds great. I've tried it before!

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: Oh? Did you try it in Inazuma?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: A few Inazuman friends made some for me.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: Haha, that's great.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: You know, I want to follow your example and travel around the world. Hopefully, I can also make good friends along the way.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Knowing you, that shouldn't be a problem.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: #That means a lot coming from you, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This should be one of the crystalline cores mentioned in the manuscript!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And here's the second one.
